title: Effects of Harvest and Fertilization Frequency on Protein Yield and Extractability from Flood-Tolerant Perennial Grasses Cultivated on a Fen Peatland
source_location: Tables 3 and 4, annual average yield rows
license: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY), as stated in the article
design: Four-block field experiment, reed canary grass and tall fescue, 2–5 harvests per year; laboratory screw pressing and acid precipitation.
units: All yield means and SDs are t/ha/year. DM fields are dry-matter mass yields; CP fields are crude-protein mass yields.
transformation: Annual-average row values and parenthetical standard deviations transcribed into separate numeric columns. Source-reported >0.0 standard deviations remain the text >0.0. No recalculation or imputation.
process_conditions: Biomass was stored overnight at 2°C and pressed the following morning at room temperature using a lab-scale twin-screw press. Juice was acidified to pH 4 with 14.8 mol/L phosphoric acid, held overnight at 4°C, and centrifuged for 12 min at 2000×g at 4°C. The article does not report the phosphoric-acid volume/equivalents in the accessible methods.
applicability: Cultivated flood-tolerant forage analogue for annual press-fraction and protein-product yield context; not direct roadside-grass/GreenHub performance.
limitations: The source reports treatment-level annual means; component-stream mean yields do not sum exactly to feed mean yield and should not be forced into a closed mass balance.
The article attributes protein-balance losses to press foaming/juice overflow and fiber residues in the press; per-stream values are not a complete measured mass balance.
Fertilization differs between one-cut and 2–5-cut treatments; this dataset includes 2–5-cut observations only, but broader cross-treatment comparisons remain confounded.
No GreenHub feed basis, scale-up law, acid dose, industrial separator performance, or product market grade is established.
The authors state raw data are available on request; only published annual-average table values are included.
